areas.summary: Studio is a free, MIT-licensed Windows app. Download the portable build or run it from source; you don't need an account.

features.name: Portable Windows download
features.what: Download the zip from GitHub Releases, extract the whole folder and open Mefi Studio AI+.exe. You don't need Node or Git to run it, and its tasks, plans and chats stay in its own resources\app\data folder.
features.evidence: README.md 'Install and run' (Portable build bullet); CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'First public release: a portable Windows build published to GitHub Releases'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Get Studio running'

features.name: Run from source
features.what: Clone the repository and run npm ci, npm run build-booklet and npm start with Node 24. On main (coming in 0.4.5), npm ci downloads Electron again, stops at once on an older Node, and the launcher downloads Electron itself when it is missing.
features.evidence: README.md 'Requirements' and 'Install and run'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice. **Install**: npm ci fetches the Electron binary again...'

features.name: One-click launcher
features.what: Double-click 'Run Mefi's Studio AI+.cmd' to start the portable build when one exists in dist/, or the source install otherwise.
features.evidence: README.md 'Install and run' (launcher bullet); file present in the v0.2.0 tree (git ls-tree v0.2.0)

features.name: One Studio at a time
features.what: Opening Studio a second time brings the window that is already open to the front. A source install and a portable build on the same Windows account share settings, keys and the project list, so only one of them runs at a time.
features.evidence: main.cjs requestSingleInstanceLock + app.on('second-instance', showWindow); README.md 'Install and run' (Portable build bullet)

features.name: What you need
features.what: Windows 10 or 11. Git is recommended so Studio can check commits and sync PCs. A coding CLI is optional; without one you can still plan and chat, but nothing can be built. Python is only needed to run the test suite.
features.evidence: README.md 'Requirements' table; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Install what Studio needs'

features.name: Browser-only preview
features.what: npm run start:web opens a look-around preview at localhost:4173. It cannot launch workers, and it listens only on this PC and serves only public files.
features.evidence: README.md 'Install and run'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] Security 'npm run start:web is loopback-only and serves an allow-list'

features.name: Free and open source (MIT)
features.what: All of Studio's code is public on GitHub under the MIT license. You can use it, fork it or change it for free.
features.evidence: LICENSE (MIT, 2026 MefiMaxi); README.md 'License'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0]

features.name: Contribute and request features on GitHub
features.what: Open an issue or a pull request. Bug reports and feature requests have their own templates, and pull requests list the three checks to pass.
features.evidence: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md (label: enhancement), bug_report.md, config.yml, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md; README.md 'Contributing'; CONTRIBUTING.md

features.name: Private security reports
features.what: Report anything that could expose keys or files privately through GitHub's vulnerability reporting instead of a public issue. You'll get an acknowledgement within a week.
features.evidence: SECURITY.md 'Reporting a vulnerability'; .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml 'Security issue' link

features.name: Runs on Linux from source (checked in CI)
features.what: Studio ships for Windows only. Every push also checks the source on Linux, where the app reaches a window. Linux and macOS are not supported or tested as desktop platforms.
features.evidence: .github/workflows/studio-linux.yml header ('ci.yml is the authority on Windows, which is where Studio ships'); README.md Requirements 'Other platforms are untested'

areas.summary: Nothing runs until you choose. A launch screen, a setup helper and a seven-stop walkthrough show a new person how to connect an AI and open a project.

features.name: Launch screen
features.what: Every launch opens on a project picker, with the last project already selected. Choose Open another folder…, then Open studio (agents stay off) or Open and start agents. You can also continue without a project.
features.evidence: README.md 'First launch' step 1; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Every launch: choose the project, then start the agents'; renderer/startup.js strings 'Open studio', 'Open and start agents', 'Continue without a project'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Project chooser on every launch'

features.name: When Studio opens
features.what: A setting in Settings › General › Profile & startup. Choose Resume what I had (the default), Start agents or Keep agents off, and the launch screen's main button follows it. Open with agents off is always one click away.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'When Studio opens'; commit 1d86a1a 'Agents say why they are not working; approvals survive late references'; renderer/startup.js 'When Studio opens', 'Open with agents off'; absent from the v0.4.4 tree

features.name: Picking up where you left off
features.what: If a crash, reboot or update restart cut work off in the last ten minutes, Studio reopens that folder and restarts the agents that were running. If you closed Studio yourself, it asks again next time.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Session continuity'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Every launch' (second paragraph); README.md 'First launch' step 1

features.name: Setup helper
features.what: One sheet holds every setting that decides what agents do. It opens first on a new install and once after an update that adds to it. Quick setup is three steps (connect an AI, choose how much Mefi may decide, finish), and Everything walks through Connect an AI, Team & models, Routing, How work runs, Permissions, Tools & skills, Machine & app and Look. Changes save as you go, and you can reopen it from Search or Help.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Setup helper' and 'Setup finds the login you have'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'First: the setup helper'; docs/architecture.md 'Getting around' (setup helper bullet); renderer/setup-helper.js SECTIONS; commits 9cb13e2 'Add the setup helper, free the Void collection, fix dead agent settings', 74dc3b1, 6a5c7be

features.name: Start here walkthrough
features.what: A seven-stop guide: Scan, Your workspace, First map, Connections, Create, Monitor and Review. Walk with me opens the real menu and highlights the control. The guide remembers your place and never creates a task or starts a build by itself. On main it skips the scan when an AI is already connected, and only one welcome shows at a time.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Seven-stop Start here walkthrough with a Walk with me coach'; README.md 'First launch' step 2; GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'One welcome at a time'

features.name: Scan what this PC has
features.what: The first stop looks for the OpenCode CLI, its linked providers and free models, and keys saved in Studio. It sends no prompt and saves nothing until you choose Use this setup. It also warns that free-tier models may use your prompts for training.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough' (Scan paragraph); renderer/onboarding.js scan points text ('Free-tier models may use prompts to improve the model...'), present at v0.2.0 and v0.4.4 (allowFreeTraining)

features.name: First map
features.what: A read-only explorer reads the selected folder and saves suggested first tasks as ideas, never as tasks. Since 0.4.4 it can run through a subscription CLI without OpenCode, and it offers connection fixes in place.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Fixed 'First map can use the selected provider and local project excerpts without OpenCode'; docs/cli-setup.md (mapping paragraph)

features.name: I have an API key or a local model server
features.what: At Scan and First map, this button takes you to Connections instead of installing a CLI. When you come back with a working key or local server, it scans again.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice' (Start here part); docs/cli-setup.md last section; README.md 'First launch' step 2; string absent from the v0.4.4 tree

features.name: New app
features.what: Use the + beside Vibe's project picker, name the app and describe it. Studio makes a folder under Mefi Apps in your home folder, starts git, opens it as the project and sends the description as the first request.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'New app beside Vibe's project picker'; docs/releases/0.4.4.md 'Start a new app in one step'; docs/architecture.md 'New app' bullet

features.name: Projects: one folder at a time
features.what: Open a folder from the launch screen or M+ at the top of the menu, and Studio scans it on your PC without an AI request. Tasks, conversations and plans stay with that project. Remove project drops it from the list without touching its files. With a worker running, Save & switch saves its progress before changing projects.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'Open your first folder'; docs/architecture.md 'Workspace and work' (Projects bullet); CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'Save & switch waits for saved progress'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'M+ opens Projects on the selected project'

features.name: Clear help when no AI is connected
features.what: Vibe shows a Connect an AI banner when no AI is connected. On main, Home, Vibe and agent status say 'No AI connected' instead of 'Waiting for you'. With no coding tool installed, Studio says to install OpenCode, Claude Code or Codex instead of retrying five times.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'A first run with no AI connected says so' (commit 6a5c7be 'New-user onboarding: say when no AI is connected...'); CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Vibe can run on its own' (Connect an AI banner, released)

features.name: Launch destination
features.what: Choose whether Studio opens on Home (or Vibe) or on the Command view. A switch that jumped to Command view after five quiet minutes is now off by default on main.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Your Studio ... Open Workspace on launch'; [0.4.2] 'Open Vibe on launch'; [Unreleased] 'No more surprise jump to Command view' (Show Command view after 5 quiet minutes, off)

features.name: The launch wisp
features.what: A small glowing wisp sits in the launch box and stays with the setup guide. It reacts to your pointer with little ASCII faces and sparks, and it pulses while setup or agents are working.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'A glowing wisp now wakes in the launch box'; docs/architecture.md 'Getting around' (wisp bullet)

areas.summary: Use a subscription you already have (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity), an API key, or a model running on your own PC. Studio doesn't sell AI access; your provider's limits apply.

features.name: Use a subscription you already have (guided CLI setup)
features.what: Pick Codex, Claude Code, Grok, Antigravity or OpenCode. Install and sign in opens a setup window that installs the tool (and Node.js if needed) and runs the vendor's sign-in. Check connection then sends one small test prompt on your account. Passwords and tokens stay with the CLI.
features.evidence: docs/cli-setup.md steps 1-3; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'Guided CLI installation, sign-in and connection checks in Start here'; docs/releases/0.4.4.md 'Use a subscription you already have'. Caveat: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Second bug-hunt pass... Guided CLI setup opens its terminal again (a detached PowerShell never ran its script)'; v0.4.4 scripts/cli-setup.cjs spawns powershell with detached:true, main has 'Not detached' fix

features.name: Use for the whole studio
features.what: One click runs chat, mapping, planning, every agent seat and the coding workers on that one signed-in account. It turns cross-provider fallback off and keeps your other saved keys and models.
features.evidence: docs/cli-setup.md step 4; README.md 'First launch' step 2; renderer/setup-helper.js providers section button 'Use for the whole studio'

features.name: Detects tools you install while Studio is open
features.what: On Windows, Studio re-reads PATH before it looks for coding CLIs, so a tool installed while Studio is open shows up without a restart. Refresh installed tools does the same by hand, and on main closing the setup window refreshes automatically.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Fixed 'Coding CLIs installed while Studio is open no longer show "not found"'; docs/cli-setup.md step 3; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'closing a setup window refreshes the tools'

features.name: More than one login
features.what: Add a second (up to a sixth) Claude Code or Codex subscription login under Setup › Connect an AI › More than one login. Studio uses the first login until it hits its usage limit, moves to the next, and returns after the reset. Nothing else answers until every login is topped out. Each login gets its own row in Usage.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'More than one Claude Code or Codex login'; docs/cli-setup.md 'More than one login'; renderer/setup-helper.js loginsCard; commit 07150aa 'Use more than one Claude Code or Codex login, swapping when one tops out'

features.name: API keys: z.ai, OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, OpenRouter
features.what: Paste a key once and it is encrypted on this PC. z.ai's GLM coding plan and OpenCode Go work since 0.2.0, OpenCode Zen since 0.3.0 and OpenRouter (free router by default) since 0.4.0. Saving a key never switches an agent to it by itself.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'Connect one assistant and one builder' table; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'OpenCode Zen is a route'; [0.4.0] 'OpenRouter as a companion provider, with the free router default'; renderer/setup-helper.js KEYS and 'API keys' card

features.name: Local models: LM Studio and any OpenAI-compatible server
features.what: Point Studio at LM Studio running on your PC, or at a custom endpoint such as Ollama. On main the custom key is optional, auto setup finds Ollama on its default port, and LM Studio only shows as ready when a model is loaded.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'multi-provider routing (... LM Studio, custom endpoint)'; docs/architecture.md 'Model Lab and routing' (AI routing bullet, Ollama http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1); CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice' (Any AI route part)

features.name: Start free with OpenCode
features.what: No subscription and no key? OpenCode's free models are a way in. The scan finds them, and on main a Start free with OpenCode button picks OpenCode for you.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Setup finds the login you have' ('Set up automatically and Start free with OpenCode'); renderer/setup-helper.js 'Start free with OpenCode'; free-model scan itself released since 0.2.0 (GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough')

features.name: Auto setup
features.what: Studio looks at saved keys, installed CLIs and local servers and picks a working setup. A fresh install runs it once by itself, and Run auto setup (or Set up automatically) runs it again. It sends no paid request, changes no keys, and says what it chose. On main it picks a signed-in Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity first and doesn't count a CLI that isn't signed in.
features.evidence: README.md 'First launch' step 3; docs/architecture.md 'Auto setup' bullet; main.cjs firstLaunchAutoSetup (commit 0bdad1b 'Auto setup on first launch', in v0.2.0); CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Setup finds the login you have'

features.name: Chat and coding are checked separately
features.what: Studio shows whether you can talk to an AI and whether a coding worker can build. A saved key alone never claims a build can start.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md '2. Connect your tools' and 'Connect one assistant and one builder'

features.name: Headless key setup
features.what: On a machine with no screen, set MEFI_STUDIO_KEY (or the z.ai, Zen, OpenRouter, gateway, Jev or custom variable) and run npx electron . --set-key once. Then remove the variable, because while it is set it overrides the saved key.
features.evidence: README.md 'Keys and privacy' bullet 1; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Connect one assistant and one builder'; .env.example; SECURITY.md 'Scope notes'

features.name: Connection details for Discord and rooms
features.what: Settings › Community › Connection details takes the Mefi Studio Link app ID and the rooms hub address once per PC. They work at once with no restart or environment variables, and Save tells you whether the hub answered.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Discord linking and Rooms without environment variables'; docs/friends-setup.md '3. Every PC'; commit 6b633be 'Link Discord and reach the rooms hub without environment variables'

features.name: Your own MCP tools
features.what: Register trusted local MCP servers in ~/.mefi-studio/mcp.json, then choose which of their tools each agent may use. Only local (stdio) servers are supported.
features.evidence: docs/agent-tools.md 'Register a trusted MCP server'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Per-agent web search, project-read permissions and MCP tool allowlists'

areas.summary: Choose which AI answers each role, what happens when one fails, and which model builds each task. You can also let Studio choose for you.

features.name: Automatic provider order
features.what: Roles on Automatic try your providers in the order you set. You can reorder, add or remove providers in Routing.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Model Lab and routing' (AI routing bullet); renderer/setup-helper.js routing section 'Automatic provider order'; commit a096d94 'Add project-first startup and ordered auto routing' (v0.2.0)

features.name: Signed-in coding tools first
features.what: When it's on (the default), Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity logins answer before your listed providers, so subscriptions you already pay for are used first.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'plus a subscription-first switch'; renderer/setup-helper.js toggle 'Try signed-in coding tools first'; docs/architecture.md AI routing bullet

features.name: Fall back when a provider fails
features.what: An opt-in switch sends a failed or rate-limited call to the next provider in the order instead of waiting.
features.evidence: renderer/setup-helper.js toggle 'Fall back when a provider fails'; docs/architecture.md AI routing bullet ('the opt-in fallback walks down the list')

features.name: Saved keys work without reordering
features.what: On main, a key you saved for a provider that isn't in the order (z.ai, OpenCode Go, Zen, OpenRouter or custom) still answers when nothing listed can, so saving a key never needs a routing change.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md AI routing bullet; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice' ('a saved OpenRouter, Zen or custom key works on Auto without editing the order')

features.name: Failing providers pause instead of stalling
features.what: After three failures in a row a provider is paused for 30 seconds, and the next one answers straight away. Saving a key or changing routing lifts the pause at once.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Changed 'A model route that keeps failing is paused instead of retried every turn'; [0.4.4] 'Changing an AI route or credential releases the previous provider's retry backoff'

features.name: Outages don't cost a task its tries
features.what: When a provider hits a usage limit, rate limit or outage, the task waits and retries later without losing one of its attempts.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Fixed 'A provider outage (usage limit, rate limit, API unreachable) no longer spends a card's tries'

features.name: Different AI for chat and for planning
features.what: Routine answers (chat, quick checks) and planning & review (plans, briefs, reviews) can each use their own provider and model, with reasoning effort where the model supports it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Added 'Planning and reading can each answer through their own provider'; renderer/setup-helper.js roleRow 'Assistant · routine' / 'Assistant · planning & review'

features.name: Teams: Studio defaults, project teams and saved teams
features.what: Agents › Setup edits a team as a draft with Apply changes or Discard draft. Every project uses Studio defaults until you give it its own team. Save a team as a preset to reuse it; a preset is an independent copy.
features.evidence: docs/unified-studio.md 'Agents' (Apply changes, Discard draft, presets); renderer/setup-helper.js 'Saved teams'; agentTeams present from v0.4.0

features.name: Agent seats
features.what: The companion, context scout, overseer, lead and desk can each run on their own model, with effort and fast-mode settings. Seats only send text, so Grok, Codex and Antigravity aren't offered for them.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Seats' and 'Agents setup now includes companion, scout, overseer and subtask routing'; renderer/setup-helper.js SEATS and SEAT_BLOCKED

features.name: Models saved per provider, with live model lists
features.what: Each provider and each coding CLI keeps its own model choice, so switching never mixes them. Refresh model list fetches a provider's current models (OpenRouter shows free ones first), or you can type a model ID.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'Models are saved per provider and per builder CLI'; docs/architecture.md routing bullets; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'searchable provider model lists'; docs/unified-studio.md 'Use Refresh model list'

features.name: Choose your coding worker
features.what: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity can edit your project, and split-off subtasks can follow it or use another tool. On main, builds from any of these are checked by Studio's own verification instead of being sent back to OpenCode.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Settings & connections ... Grok / Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity CLIs'; docs/architecture.md 'Builders run through...' bullet; renderer/setup-helper.js 'Subtask builders'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice' (Any builder part)

features.name: Coding tiers: Auto, Free, Fast, Heavy
features.what: Decide what each build may cost. Auto picks per task, Free uses free models one worker at a time and never falls back to paid ones, Fast uses quick economical models, and Heavy uses the strongest. Settings shows what each tier will run before anything starts.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'coding tiers (Auto / Free / Fast / Heavy)'; docs/architecture.md 'A coding tier...' bullet; renderer/booklet.template.html tier options

features.name: Picks the model most likely to succeed
features.what: Under Auto, Studio records which models passed verification for each kind of work and gives the build to the one most likely to succeed, weighing cost, speed and headroom. A model you pin always wins.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md coding tier bullet (win probability, agent-loop.md §12); winProbability present from the v0.4.0 tree; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'A builder model you pin runs, whatever the route'

features.name: Try again with a heavier model
features.what: Re-run a task's next attempt on the builder's Heavy-tier model. On main it is only offered where such a model exists.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Try again with a heavier model' bullet; string present at v0.2.0; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice' fix

features.name: Jev model selection
features.what: Choose Automatic, where a small decision model called Jev sorts new work and helps pick models, or Fixed, which always uses your chosen models. Jev runs through the Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenCode Zen or OpenRouter with its own key. It's optional: without it Studio uses fixed defaults.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'Jev model selection needs a key'; docs/architecture.md 'Settings › Decision model'; renderer/setup-helper.js 'Jev, the decision model' and JEV_ROUTES; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Jev routes'

features.name: Plain-language connection errors
features.what: A Claude quota or login problem shows the CLI's real message and reset time instead of 'claude error: success'. On main, a missing tool reads 'x is not installed or not on PATH'.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Claude connection errors show the actual quota or login message'; [Unreleased] 'A first run with no AI connected says so'

areas.summary: See what each plan and key has left, and what Studio spent today, without sending any prompts.

features.name: Usage popover
features.what: The Usage pill in the corner of the Command view opens one card per plan, with a bar and reset time for each window, plus balances and today's calls. The pill shows the plan closest to running out.

features.name: Subscription limits read from your own logins
features.what: Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity plan windows are read through each CLI's own login, with no prompt sent and no credentials read. These checks only run while you're looking.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The coding CLIs are read through their own logins with no prompt and no credential read'; docs/architecture.md 'Through each coding CLI's own login'

features.name: Balances and credits
features.what: See OpenCode Go's 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows, z.ai plan credits, OpenRouter's balance and free allowance, the Vercel AI Gateway balance, whether LM Studio is up, and priced Zen calls.

features.what: A daily tally by provider and model of Studio's own calls and the coding sessions' turns. Subscription calls show as unpriced rather than free.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Usage tracker per day, provider and model'; docs/architecture.md 'Usage tracker sums two ledgers'

features.name: Speed probe
features.what: Measure a model's tokens per second with one small request from Settings › System › Diagnostics.
features.evidence: renderer/booklet.template.html #settings-diagnostics 'Speed probe', 'Measure tokens/s'; present at v0.2.0

areas.summary: Studio is local-first. It has no account, no telemetry and encrypted keys, and it only talks to the AI services and tools you connect.

features.name: Local-first projects
features.what: Tasks, conversations, plans and settings stay on your PC. They are never committed to Git or packed into a release. Studio's own files never touch your project's files unless an agent builds a task there.
features.evidence: README.md 'What it does' (Local storage bullet) and 'Keys and privacy'; SECURITY.md 'Local state is never committed or packaged'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'release zips carry no local data'

features.name: No account, no telemetry
features.what: There's no sign-up and no usage tracking. Studio only contacts the providers and CLIs you connect, GitHub's release API, media services you play, and Discord or the rooms hub if you choose to link them.
features.evidence: SECURITY.md 'No telemetry, no hosted account'; README.md badge 'local-first · no telemetry'

features.name: Encrypted keys, never shown back
features.what: Keys are encrypted with the Windows keystore (DPAPI) in their own file, separate from your preferences. The app only ever shows 'saved' or 'not saved', and a key only works for the Windows account that saved it.
features.evidence: SECURITY.md 'Keys stay on your machine'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Keys are encrypted with the Windows keystore ... auth.json'; commit 2457a7d 'Split saved-key ciphertext into auth.json beside settings.json' (v0.3.0)

features.name: Keys stay out of agents' reach
features.what: Coding workers, git, npm, verification checks and other child processes don't get Studio's saved keys in their environment.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Security 'Coding workers no longer inherit Studio's own keys'; [0.3.3] Security 'Child processes no longer inherit Studio's keys'; [0.4.0] Fixed 'Verification checks no longer see Studio's API keys'

features.name: Secrets masked in logs
features.what: Tool transcripts and scout payloads are cleaned of secrets, and Authorization: Bearer tokens are masked before they are saved.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] bug-hunt 'Privacy: tool transcripts and scout payloads are redacted before JSON-escaping, and Authorization: Bearer tokens are masked'

features.name: Chat through a CLI runs with its tools off
features.what: When a subscription CLI answers chat, planning or mapping, it runs in a throwaway folder with its file, shell and MCP tools turned off. Only coding workers edit your project.
features.evidence: docs/cli-setup.md 'Text adapters run outside the project in disposable directories...'; scripts/cli-text.cjs (first in the v0.4.4 tree)

features.name: The window stays on its own page
features.what: Links open in your normal browser, and only http and https links. Nothing can navigate the Studio window away from the app.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] Security 'The Studio window never leaves its own page' and 'shell:open opens only http and https links'; SECURITY.md 'Scope notes'

features.name: You decide what agents may do
features.what: Agents run real commands in the folder you choose. Pick a permission mode: Always ask, Accept per task, Auto (the default) or Elevated only. Always ask makes every new task wait for your OK.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'Four saved permission modes'; docs/architecture.md 'Permission modes'; SECURITY.md 'Agents run real commands'; README.md 'Keys and privacy' (Verify first)

features.name: Web search and file reads are per agent
features.what: Choose which agents may search the web (queries leave your PC) and which may read project files. Project reads are off by default and skip credential files.
features.evidence: docs/agent-tools.md (web search and project reads paragraphs); CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Per-agent web search, project-read permissions'

features.name: Discord stays optional
features.what: Nothing contacts Discord until you choose Link my Discord. The link reads only your Discord id, names and roles in the Void Engine server, never your projects. Unlink revokes it. Releases don't ship the link app ID yet, so linking needs it entered first.
features.evidence: SECURITY.md 'Optional Discord link'; docs/community.md; scripts/community.cjs CLIENT_ID = "" and scripts/hub-client.cjs HUB_URL = "" (not configured in builds); CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Discord linking and Rooms without environment variables'

features.name: Settings that don't get lost
features.what: Settings saves wait their turn so two changes never undo each other. A damaged settings file is copied aside instead of being wiped, and damaged task stores are recovered instead of reset.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] Fixed 'Settings saves no longer undo each other' and 'A settings.json that stops parsing is copied aside'; [0.4.4] 'Torn store files with multi-field records are salvaged'

features.name: Actions that can't be undone ask twice
features.what: Deleting, removing keys, stopping workers, Stop all, Restart and similar actions share one two-step button: the first press asks and the second does it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Actions that can't be undone ask twice'; commit 049904c 'One two-step confirm and one plain error sentence for every menu'

areas.summary: The portable app can find and install new releases itself. Source installs pick up changes as you edit.

features.name: In-app release updates
features.what: The portable app checks GitHub every 20 minutes, and you can press Check GitHub in Settings › System › Updates. Update downloads the new build, verifies it, waits for running builds to finish, then replaces the app files after Studio exits and relaunches. Your data folder is never touched.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Release updates'; renderer/booklet.template.html #settings-updates ('Check GitHub', 'Update'); main.cjs applyReleaseUpdate ('build job(s) still running'). Caveat: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'the release updater's install helper now actually runs after Studio exits'; the v0.4.4 main.cjs spawns the helper as a detached PowerShell, which main's fix comment says 'exits at once without running its script, so the update never applied'

features.name: Checked downloads
features.what: Every update is checked against its published SHA-256. A mismatch or an unreadable checksum stops the update and removes the download.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'in-app updater that verifies the published SHA-256'; [0.3.3] Security 'Updates are checked against their published SHA-256'

features.name: Update badge and notices
features.what: The menu shows an update badge, and a toast says 'Update available · vX' or 'Updated to vX'. The Update button can't start a second download.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'the update badge and the update toasts open Settings › Updates'; renderer/nav.js releaseToast; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] bug-hunt 'Updates' fixes

features.name: Updates for private copies
features.what: If you run from a private fork, save a read-only GitHub token in Settings › System › Updates, set MEFI_STUDIO_GITHUB_TOKEN, or let Studio reuse the GitHub CLI's sign-in.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Release updates' (second paragraph); GETTING_STARTED.md 'Private release updates'

features.name: Live update for source installs
features.what: A source install watches its own files. Style changes apply in place, pages reload and keep your view, and main-process changes restart the app. A broken file puts the update on hold instead of crashing.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Live update'; renderer/booklet.template.html 'Apply updates automatically'

features.name: Restart now saves your agents first
features.what: Restart now stops the coding agents, saves their latest work, checklist and output, then relaunches Studio paused. Resume carries on.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Update's Restart now stops coding agents, saves their latest work for continuation'; docs/architecture.md 'Live update' (third paragraph)

features.name: Fresh model catalog with each update
features.what: Installed apps receive the updated public model catalog along with the new version.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] bug-hunt 'installed apps receive the new model catalog'

features.name: Friends › Your PCs
features.what: See whether this PC matches the project's default branch on GitHub, and what hasn't reached it: uncommitted files, unpushed commits, stashes, worktrees and local branches. Opening it only looks.

features.name: Sync this PC
features.what: Pulls what your other PCs pushed and pushes this PC's commits, never by force and never over uncommitted work. On main it only pushes after the project's own npm run check passes.

features.name: Put my commits on top of GitHub's

features.name: Friends badge and a question on close

features.what: One private GitHub repository, <you>/mefi-studio-vault, carries what you tick between your own PCs, sealed with AES-256-GCM so GitHub can't read it. You can share model results, what Studio learned, agent teams, brains, Playbook recipes, Claude Code memory notes, preferences, and open tasks and ideas. Everything is checked on the way out and on the way in, and nothing you already have is overwritten.

notes:
I checked status against the published trees, not only the changelog. This is a read-only report: I changed no files. Evidence cites origin/main because another session is editing CHANGELOG.md in the working tree.

1. Some features look like 0.4.4 but did not ship in it. Several [Unreleased] changelog entries come from commits that are ancestors of the v0.4.4 tag: 27413e2 (companion pet), 5d47154 (Configuration, Habits, motion), fc47258 (sync hardening), de7a3bc (Set up this PC), 2dd1ff8 (first-time setup fixes), 215b7d9 (bug hunt). But the 16:57 merge (65703a6) and 7ba162c dropped that code before 0.4.4 was built. dc85f68 restored it and says "0.4.4 was built without them". I confirmed this in the v0.4.4 tree: renderer/config-dialog.js, companion-friends.js, motion.js, setup-helper.js and pc-vault.js are missing, and so are the strings 'Put my commits on top', 'Set up this PC', 'Interface scale', 'Resume what I had' and 'I have an API key or a local model server'. So `git describe --contains` shows v0.4.4 for these, but they are coming in 0.4.5. The changelog is correct to list them as Unreleased.

2. Two setup windows in the 0.4.4 download are probably broken. Both are fixed on main. The owner should test on a real 0.4.4 install before the site makes any promise.
   - **Guided CLI setup:** In the v0.4.4 scripts/cli-setup.cjs, Install and sign in / Sign in launch PowerShell as a detached process. Main's fix comment says such a window "gets no console and exits at once". So 0.4.4 users may need to install and sign in to the CLI in a terminal themselves; Check connection and Use for the whole studio should still work after that.
   - **Release updater:** Every release from v0.2.0 through v0.4.4 launches its install helper as a detached PowerShell. Main's comment says it "exits at once without running its script, so the update never applied" (changelog: "the release updater's install helper now actually runs after Studio exits"). So the site should not promise a one-click in-app update from 0.4.4 to 0.4.5. It should tell people to download and extract 0.4.5 and keep their resources\app\data folder.

3. Labels have drifted. README says to check "App updates", and dist/promo pages say "Settings › Updates & diagnostics"; the real path is Settings › System › Updates (Check GitHub / Update). The setup helper's "Install updates automatically" switch actually saves the source-install live updater's auto-apply setting (updateSet auto), not release installs, so word it carefully. README's First launch section doesn't mention the 0.4.5 setup helper; GETTING_STARTED.md already describes it. GETTING_STARTED "Review the defaults" says useWeb is on by default, but the code defaults it to off.

4. Rolling-out means built but not live. Builds ship with an empty Discord link app ID (scripts/community.cjs CLIENT_ID = "") and an empty hub address (scripts/hub-client.cjs HUB_URL = ""). On main, each PC can enter them in Settings › Community › Connection details. Discord linking, rooms, Listen together, Friends playdates and cowork file claims all depend on this.

5. Planned, not built. The schema has no "planned" status, so this is left out of the list: the "Hey Studio" voice popup is only a proposal (docs/public-site.md; mic input only drives the audio visualiser, no speech-to-text). README also calls in-app cowork rooms future work for 0.4.4; on main they exist as Rooms plus claims but are rolling-out.

6. What's not supported, for an honest limits section:
   - Windows only. Other platforms are untested; Linux is only checked in CI, and there is no macOS build.
   - Release updates install only into the packaged Windows build, and guided CLI install only runs on Windows.
   - The browser preview cannot run workers.
   - Keys can't be copied between PCs through auth.json (on main, the vault's keys shelf does this).
   - Only one of the source and portable installs runs at a time.
   - Git worktrees can't live on exFAT or FAT drives.
   - MCP supports only local stdio servers: no remote HTTP/SSE, no OAuth.
   - Grok, Codex and Antigravity can't fill text seats, and Grok and Antigravity builders don't get Studio's tool bridge.
   - Studio doesn't provide AI access; provider limits apply. Free-tier models may use prompts for training.
   - The Studio tool checkboxes don't restrict a coding CLI's own tools (docs/agent-tools.md).

7. For the "request a feature" part of the site: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md already exists (label: enhancement), and config.yml links the getting-started guide and private security reporting.

8. Wiki pages in this scope that need 0.4.5 updates: installation.md, connections.md, updates.md, privacy.md, troubleshooting.md, getting-started.md and whats-new.md in C:\wt\site\wiki\pages. They are written for 0.4.4 and don't cover the setup helper, More than one login, When Studio opens, Connection details, Interface scale, Configuration, or the Your PCs additions (Set up this PC, Keep this PC up to date, rebase, close prompt, vault, Share with friends).
